hints: Look carefully at the y-axis. A positive change in volume of solution means water has left the tissue and entered the solution. What does the flat, plateau part from 0.80 to 1.00 $mol\ dm^{-3}$ tell you?

Remember water always moves from higher water potential to lower water potential by osmosis, but a plant cell can only lose a limited amount of water before the protoplast pulls fully away from the wall.
walkthrough:
**Read what the graph is really showing**

Think side by side with me. The y-axis is change in volume of solution, not mass of tissue.

If the value is negative, the solution got smaller, so water moved into the tissue. If the value is positive, the solution got bigger, so water moved out of the tissue into the solution.

**Find where there is no net movement**

No net movement means change = 0. On the graph this is where the line crosses the x-axis, at about 0.22 $mol\ dm^{-3}$.

That crossing point tells us the external solution has the same water potential as the tissue. From 0.80 to 1.00 $mol\ dm^{-3}$ the change is about +1.3 $cm^3$, so lots of water has left the tissue. Statement 1 is false.

**Explain the flat plateau from 0.80 to 1.00**

From 0.50 to 0.80 the curve rises as more concentrated solution draws out more water. Then from 0.80 to 1.00 it goes flat.

Increasing the salt concentration further causes no extra water loss. That means there is no more free water left to lose. The protoplast is fully pulled away from the cell wall, the cells are fully plasmolysed. Statement 3 is true and statement 2 is false because living plant tissue always has solutes, so its water potential is negative, never zero.

options.A: Both statements are false. There was net movement out of the tissue (positive change) and tissue water potential is negative, not zero.
options.B: Statement 1 is false because the +1.3 cm3 change shows water did move out. Statement 3 alone is true, so this combination is wrong.
options.C: Statement 2 is false. Only pure water has a water potential of zero. Plant tissue contains solutes so its water potential is negative.
options.D: Only statement 3 is correct. The plateau shows no further water loss despite higher external concentration, because cells are already fully plasmolysed.
